prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1233; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On the day of the incident, I was dispatched to an intersection in League City, Texas, where a two-vehicle collision had been reported. Driver 1 stated that they were making a left turn when their vehicle was struck by Driver 2's vehicle. Driver 2 gave a statement consistent with that account and said the contact occurred as Driver 1 turned across their path. Both vehicles remained in the roadway when I arrived. An independent witness at the corner confirmed the sequence of events, and photographs taken at the scene show the contact points on both vehicles. The damage to Driver 1's vehicle is generally consistent with the reported impact. Passenger was seated in Driver 1's vehicle at the time of the collision and was identified by both drivers and the witness. Driver 1 reported pain in the right wrist and was evaluated by emergency medical personnel on scene. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was known to either party or noted during the inspection. Driver 1 provided proof of insurance listing them as a named driver on the policy. No citations were issued at the scene.
